Programming Language: Laravel 10+ PHP 8.2, RESTful API, MySQL, OAuth2
Original Requirements: Build the Volopa OOP (Out-of-Pocket) Expenses API System covering User Management, Pocket Expense CSV Batch Upload, and Single Expense Data Capturing with role-based permissions, CSV validation, and FX conversion capabilities.
Product Goals: Implement hierarchical role-based access control with delegation capabilities
Provide robust CSV batch upload with synchronous all-or-nothing validation
Enable single expense capture with flexible metadata and approval workflow
Integrate real-time FX conversion with client commission adjustments
Ensure secure API endpoints with OAuth2 authentication
Support audit trails for permission grants and expense operations
Deliver high-performance bulk operations with queue-based processing
Maintain data integrity through comprehensive validation rules
User Stories: As a Primary Administrator, I want to grant management rights to Administrator users so they can manage specific subsets of users
As an Administrator with management rights, I want to create, view, update, and approve expenses for my managed users
As a Business User with management rights, I want to create, view, and update expenses for users I manage but cannot approve them
As any user, I want to create, view, update, and delete my own out-of-pocket expenses
As an Administrator, I want to upload a CSV file with up to 200 expense records for a selected user with immediate validation feedback
As a system user, I want to receive structured error messages when CSV validation fails, showing line numbers and specific field errors
As an Administrator, I want to download validation errors as CSV for reference and correction
As a user creating expenses, I want automatic FX conversion based on my wallet's base currency with real-time rate updates
As a user, I want to override the system-calculated converted amount if needed
As an expense creator, I want to attach receipts and add metadata like categories, tracking codes, and projects to my expenses
As a user, I want to track expense status through draft, submitted, approved, and rejected states
As an Administrator, I want to configure custom expense sources for my organization up to 20 active sources
As a system administrator, I want comprehensive audit logs of all permission grants, revokes, and expense operations
As an API consumer, I want consistent JSON response formats with proper HTTP status codes
As a mobile app user, I want all API endpoints to work seamlessly with OAuth2 authentication
Competitive Analysis: Expensify: Strong mobile app, receipt scanning, but limited role delegation features
Concur SAP: Enterprise-grade approval workflows, but complex setup and expensive
Ramp: Excellent real-time spending controls, but focused mainly on corporate cards
Brex: Good expense management with FX handling, but limited permission granularity
Zoho Expense: Affordable with basic CSV import, but lacks advanced validation features
QuickBooks Online: Strong accounting integration, but weak multi-user permission system
Xero: Good API capabilities and reporting, but limited batch upload validation

Requirement Analysis: The Volopa OOP Expenses system requires a sophisticated multi-module Laravel API that handles complex permission hierarchies, bulk data processing, and real-time financial calculations. The system must support role-based access control where Primary Administrators can delegate management rights to Administrator users, who then manage subsets of users. The CSV batch upload feature demands synchronous validation of up to 200 rows with all-or-nothing processing, requiring robust error handling and structured feedback. The single expense capture module needs flexible metadata storage, approval workflows, and FX conversion with client-specific commission adjustments. All endpoints must be protected by OAuth2 middleware and follow RESTful design principles with consistent JSON responses. The system architecture emphasizes separation of concerns with thin controllers, service layer business logic, and comprehensive validation through FormRequest classes.
Requirement Pool: Implement user_feature_permission table with role hierarchy and delegation system supporting Primary Admin, Admin, Business User, and Card User roles with granular permissions
Build CSV batch upload endpoint with PocketExpenseCSVValidator service, synchronous all-or-nothing validation for max 200 rows, structured error responses, and background job processing
Create pocket_expense CRUD operations with status workflow (draft/submitted/approved/rejected), flexible metadata storage, and approval system based on user permissions
Integrate FX conversion API with 30-day lookback for dated rates, client commission adjustments, user override capability, and wallet base currency detection
Implement OAuth2 middleware protection for all endpoints with proper permission checks, audit logging, and secure request/response handling with consistent JSON API Resource formatting
UI Design draft: The system is a backend API-only solution with no frontend UI requirements. However, it supports frontend applications through well-structured JSON API endpoints. The API design follows RESTful principles with clear resource-based URLs like `/api/expenses` for CRUD operations, `/api/uploads/pocket-expense/csv` for batch upload, and `/api/permissions` for user management. Response formats use Laravel API Resources for consistent data transformation, with standardized error objects containing field-level validation messages, line numbers for CSV errors, and proper HTTP status codes (200/201/204 for success, 422 for validation, 401/403 for auth). The system supports both mobile and web clients through OAuth2 token-based authentication.
Anything UNCLEAR: All technical requirements are clearly specified. The system architecture, database schema, validation rules, and API endpoints are well-defined. The integration points with existing Volopa infrastructure (OAuth2, user tables, client tables, currency services) are documented. The permission hierarchy and delegation rules are explicit, and the CSV validation requirements with error handling are comprehensive.
